outcome.answer:
Koh et al. propose “Continual Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation,” introducing Synthetic Self-distillation (SynthSelf) to enable self-distillation for smaller models in continual learning when standard self-distillation relies on strong in-context learning. SynthSelf imitates in-distribution rewrite by outsourcing the task to a minimally larger same-family aligner, and uses off-policy supervision plus rejection sampling to provide high-quality supervision without breaking the model’s original distribution. Evaluations report SynthSelf consistently outperforming multiple off- and on-policy distillation methods across small-model scales, including acquisition and retention benchmarks. [1]

Other results focus on different self-distillation settings rather than Koh-style synthetic self-distillation for continual post-training: on-policy self-distillation without supervision (using internal consistency) is studied in U-OPSD [4]; token selection for on-policy self-distillation is addressed by bilevel Top-K selection (BiToK-SD) [5]; and self-distillation for diffusion language models uses masking-mode bidirectional KD (SelFusion) [2]. These differ in task/setting and mechanisms.
